source.quote: Greetings travelers and welcome back to Goldbound, the challenge series where our rogue Goldilocked is exploring the World of Warcraft by unlocking one zone at a time. And then in that zone, discovering new gold farms to optimize towards the purchase of a WoW token. And last episode, well, we got that WoW token and we spun for a new zone. So, welcome to the Dustwallow Marsh. The path we took to get here was across the great sea, courtesy of the Menithl Harbor to Theamore Isle boating lanes, which does mean we end up in Theamore Isle for our very first steps into Calumdor. And there is a lot to talk about in Theamore. For starters, the city it's actually here. And as long as I don't progress too far through the quest chain, it's going to stay that way. But if I quest too far, it gets blown to smithetherreens. But we do want it to stay here because there's actually a bunch of unlocks in Theamore Isle.

source.quote: Speaking of which, let's hope the farms are a little more like Swamp of Soros and get better acquainted with the zone because I think it's a good idea to start with gathering. Although, for this test and first zone exploration, I am running herbalism only rather than dual gathering. The reason? Well, I may just have my second perfection slot filled with something else that I don't really want to drop while I'm in the zone, but more on that later. First things first, from looking around at the herbalism nodes, though, I do think it will probably beat out Dual Gathering. There's about five types of herbs that we can get here, and they can be quite valuable. There is strangle kelp, which is actually more so out and around the waters, but it does have a solid market value of about 10 gold each at the moment, although it used to be quite a bit higher. There's also fade leaf and Khadgar's Whisker, both with a value of 15 gold each. Then there's Earthroot and King's Blood, the lower value herbs of the zone, around 5 to six gold each, but the gold standard here in the marsh is most definitely going to be Gold Thorn, coming in at a whopping 30 to 40 gold each. So, those are most definitely the major targets here. And with the first laps around the zone, the route is pretty simple. It's a big loop for the most part. Of course, trying to stay clear of the borders. Speaking of which, we don't want an unauthorized zone exploration. But now that we're on Calumdor, if we do, the forfeit zone would be Deep Holm. But after testing the borders on my main, I am happy to say that all of the borders in this zone appear to be pretty well coded and pretty reasonable on when you actually leave dust wallow and enter the barrens or Thousand Needles. Well, actually, Dustallow Marsh extends farther than expected into Thousand Needles. But since we have the marsh first, that doesn't matter for us. Flying around though, we have a few looks at some of the rares of the zone, and there's quite a few around the zone. As I fly, I'll keep tagging any ones I see. The likes of Hayok, Terramac, and of course, Dart.

source.quote: There's a total of 20 named rare spawns here as well. So, when flying around, it is definitely not uncommon to run into a few of them and to have a few rare scanner add-on dings for us to tag. Speaking of rares, there are a few higher priority rares in the zone, but for the most part, the rares here have a very solid low to mid-range transmog on their loot tables. the kinds that land squarely in the 1 to 4,000 gold range with moderate to slow sale rates. And while flying around and gathering herbs for the test, speaking of rares in the zone, check out this guy. You need something? Nat Pegle. While not a rare that we can kill, I actually completely forgot he was here. But greetings, traveler. Nat Pegle is the legendary fisherman of World of Warcraft. For example, remember that fishing rod that we won in Stranglethorn? Well, the tool tip literally reads that it was likely used by none other than Nat Pegle. But he isn't just here for show. He actually has a quest. The reward, another fishing rod. So, he does want us to fish up four rare fish and bring them back to him. Awesome. But we only have two out of four zones unlocked. So, while we can do the Swamp of Soros, Mahi Mahi, and the Savage Coast Bluegill sail fin, we will need to wait for later unlocks to get the Feralis and Desolus drops. But quest accepted and we can add that to the personal quests for Goldie. Although we were doing an hour of testing for herbalism here. So before we get too sidetracked by some side quests, let's talk about the numbers. The hall, well 45 fade leaf, 60 Khadgar's whiskers, 51 Earthroot, 32 King's Blood, and 54 Gold Thornne. The region market value average on that comes out to 4,110 gold per hour. Honestly, I was hoping it might be a little bit higher with the gold thorn prices, but the density is just quite low. And after the first 5 to 10 minutes or so, we end up flying for a long time between herb spawns. So, with that in mind, we probably will have to test out dual gathering after all. But not right now, because next, well, we have a skinning farm, and it has to do with the slumbering dragon in the middle of the zone. Welcome to Enixia's layer.

source.quote: So, if we head there, we can enter the instance, but much like Molten Core, we don't necessarily want to kill Enixia right away. Instead, there might be a little bit of a trash farm angle. As for trash, there's only about five dragon kin in Anixia's layer, at least in retail. Sometime around the rework of Inexia's layer, the trash mobs actually reduced, but the reduction in trash isn't all that it did. Strangely enough, these ads are actually coded with northern loot tables. So, as we're killing through here, I'm actually getting frostweave cloth and some northern greens. So, we technically have access to some new northern mats. Unfortunately, we can't train northern tailoring or enchanting until we get trainers in Northern. So, this will just be raw materials that we'll sell on the auction house for now and not for too much. So, are we just cloth farming here for trash? Well, not exactly. Because the dragon kin, well, they're skinnable even without northern skinning. Because on the very first skinning attempt, we just default learn the ability for northern skinning as long as we already have classic skinning trained. But after quite a bit of testing, these mobs are actually really weird for skinning.

source.quote: I just don't want to kill her early because if we do, we can no longer reset the trash and would lose out on this, well, let's be honest, quite nice little farm. But the skinning doesn't stop here in the swamp because in addition to the dragon kin flying around and running around which do have some decent leather, we also have all kinds of different beasts. All of which have different angles and potential bonuses for farming. And with it being early into the zone, I know which one I want to farm. So up in the northern area of the zone around one of the rares that I was talking about, Dart, are some more beasts. Of course, while farming in this zone though, we may just see dart, an easy tag and kill. Like most of the rares around here, though, there's no one massive item on his loot tables. The best would likely be the pillagers gloves with a market value around 13,000 gold. But what's around him are a whole bunch of raptors. And due to the level of the zone, these guys fall squarely in the heavy leather and thick leather band. So, even at maxed 300 skinning, we can get heavy leather and maybe more importantly, heavy hide. This is massive because this band has some of the most valuable skins in classic, especially heavy hide being a massive hitter at 100 to 150 gold, especially compared to most of our old historical skinning farms like sunken temple or turtle farming where we only got heavy hide while leveling up and when our skinning was level 175 to 220. But due to the levels here, we can consistently get it. The only downside, we can't really farm these guys repeatedly because they're on a regular spawn, not a hyper spawn. But it's definitely worth coming up here to check and to clear out all the raptors for a chance at heavy hides and especially if Darts around to get a kill on him. But if Dart's around, it is worth checking around for Dart's nest as well because his nest can spawn in about five locations around the raptors. But it's kind of like the wetlands razor maw egg from the cave.

source.quote: Cuz if the nest is here, we can grab the egg and gain the battle pet of the darting hatchling. And this thing has a value between 1,000 and 10,000 gold with a likely sale of probably closer to 5,000. But it's good to add onto the auction house shelves. Matter of fact, as you can tell, I already have five of them for sale. And with so many, we can add one as Goldie's zone pet. So, hello dart. And this pet has a pretty cool passive, being a darting hatchling. Every now and then he runs around like crazy. Well, I guess darts around like crazy. Pretty cool little pet to have, but not a super consistent leather farm since we have to wait for respawns. So, we'll have to wait to find a better overworld skinning farm to do while waiting for Enixia layer resets. But first, one other thing that I do believe it's time to test out and double check or at least check in the first place is if it's going to be worth it or not to do dual gathering because we've already tested herb only. And while herbs were pretty valuable, it wasn't anything too wild and came in right around 4,100 gold per hour. So my thought is that maybe with the increased ore density between minerals and herbs with mining in the mix, the gold per hour may just improve substantially. I mean, we have to test it, don't we? Leveling up mining, though, isn't particularly trivial in this zone. We need about 175 mining to gather the myithal nodes that can spawn in the zone. Now, this ends up being one or two hours of flying around getting lower than regular rates of ore.

source.quote: Ideally, we would have had some copper ore and tins stockpiled in the bank, so we could just smelt this to power level mining. But once we're on level for mining and dust wallow, we're looking at tin, iron ore, and mithril, which historically the zones that gave us Myithil ore, like Burning Steps, and Searing Gorge ended up being quite good on the gold per hour. Unfortunately here, after some initial testing, Dust wallow is not a mining angle. Mining only ended up being an abysmal 1,100 gold per hour. And even once paired with herbalism, it only ended up netting 4,400 gold per hour. So, still better than herbalism alone. But when you take into account that mining and herbalism means we have to drop skinning and lose out on our juicy Enixia's layer resets, it doesn't really seem worth the squeeze. One thing that is worth the squeeze though and that can be quite profitable from gathering, dual gathering or solo herbalism is the treasure chests in the zone. We have quite a few treasure chest spawn locations here. Of course, being an outlaw rogue track treasure enabled.

source.quote: Like the dark iron crafted gear and imperial plate sets, plus the lock banana barkin rugs, we still have quite a few of those in stock. So until we need him again, golden path can rest. But with a dark iron farmed and everything restocked, I think it's time to explore one of the new professions that Dust Wallow unlocked for us, archaeology. So we have the skill of archaeology, which gives us a new journal tab and access to a whole bunch of different factions artifacts, plus a list of completed artifacts, which is currently zero. We'll work our way through these artifacts and unlock more and more and rare ones as we go. But the main thing for now to progress is the dig sites. There's going to be four dig sites at all times per continent. Over on Calumor, we only have Dustella Marsh unlocked and none of the dig sites are there. So, it's back over the drink to Eastern Kingdoms because here we have a few available to go for. Looking at the map, there's one in the northern area of the wetlands up by Dun Modair, which might be a little bit sketchy. Plus one down in Blasted Lands, just north of Dreadm Post, and then finally a third one in Stranglethorn Veil. I'll think I'll start down in the south at Stranglethorn Veil and get heading over there. Back in Strangle Thorn Veil for a little bit of archaeology. So, with the archaeology skill, when in the vicinity of a dig site, as you can see on our mini map, there is a small red area that we can dig in. To do so, all we have to do is use the survey ability, which then spawns a telescope that points us in the direction of treasure. If the light is red, it's far, yellow is medium distance, and green, we're almost right on the money. We just repeatedly cast it until we're bang on the money or a light bulb appears. And then once we dig, we have an artifact. This one is a troll ruins. So, the artifacts we get are troll fragments, which conveniently get logged into our archaeology book, and it keeps track of each of the different types of fragments that we can work towards artifacts on. The higher level archaeology we are, the better chance we have at getting uncommon or rare artifacts to work towards. The troll we're working towards right now is just junk quality and will likely just be vendored. Notably, each dig site has eight total artifacts, or the fragments that we can dig up, and each of these nodes actually gives us a ton of XP. We are kind of power leveling on Goldie doing this. And once we have enough fragments to make the artifact, we get a random new one in the journal. There's no skipping and this is purely RNG. The idea though is the higher level archaeology we are, the better crafts we can get. But like I said, it's all random. And for the most part, all the rewards here are going to be soulbound toys, mounts, or gears. And so rather than a gold farm, it's a little more account progression for Goldie.

source.quote: And this requires just three regular salt to cure, which we can just get pretty much for free from trade good vendors. And with the current prices of heavyhide, it makes it a lot more profitable. About 70 gold to nearly 140. Very nice. So, we can improve the profits a little bit on the leather, but what about the herbs? Well, for that I need to do it on Goldie because I have to unlearn and relearn a new profession. And out of herbalism and skinning, skinning is the easier one to abandon because we can just power level it back up in wetlands in about 20 minutes. So, I can unlearn that and grab inscription. We only need level one inscription for this hustle because we're milling courtesy of Theodin here. So all of the herbs in our zone except gold thorn and I guess strangle kelp, but we don't get too much of that actually turn a modest profit once mil into either emerald pigments, indigo pigments, dusky pigments, or orange like Khadgar's whisker here. Now this will vary pretty wildly based on the day and the markets for pigments versus herbs, but I have been getting a relatively consistent 3 to four gold per herb markup here. And after milling down our herb backlog, we have a small fortune on pigments. Love to see it. Now all that's left to do is to continue doing laps undercut scans just to see how much gold we can juice here. So after a bit more farming, let's have a look at the hall. And out of curiosity, I have been running the zone timer add-on the last couple of zones. And right now we're over 38 hours in the marsh and over 8 hours in Enixia's layer.
